decisions.reason: Requiring 3.3V and 5V rails does not change the existing requirement to monitor current on both rails.
The source reaffirms the need for a 3.3V rail but does not change DCDC1 voltage, rating, compensation, or load coverage.
The source requires a 5V rail but does not change its converter, enable control, powered loads, rating, or operating policy.
Simultaneous charging and operation does not entail any change to the established battery-protection functions or thresholds.
The charging and rail requirements do not change the battery NTC interface or thermal-protection behavior.
The source concerns power-path capabilities and does not change how battery-charge status is presented or connected.
The source does not alter the panel button connector, PWRON connection, board location, or control behavior.
Continued consideration of the AXP2101 does not change the existing exposed-pad heat-transfer requirement.
The source does not resolve or change the battery connector family, pitch, pin count, pin functions, part number, or pin order.
The source addresses battery-powered operation and system rails, not the separate USB-only standalone supply path.
Requiring system-level 3.3V and 5V rails does not select an LED supply rail or change the LED data interface.
The generic rail requirement does not change the buzzer type, selected part, voltage compatibility, or sourcing policy.
